description: Detected go func() spawned without context.Context cancellation or sync.WaitGroup tracking.
suggested_fix: Pass context.Context into worker goroutines, bound concurrency with a worker pool or errgroup.Group, and await completion on shutdown.
title: Unbounded Goroutine Spawn Without Context or WaitGroup Lifecycle
why_it_matters: Fire-and-forget goroutines can block forever on network/channel I/O (leaking heap memory) or get terminated mid-execution on SIGTERM.

description: Detected goroutine mutating shared state (++, --, +=) without sync.Mutex or sync/atomic synchronization.
suggested_fix: Protect shared state with sync.Mutex (mu.Lock()/defer mu.Unlock()) or use sync/atomic (atomic.Int64).
title: Unsynchronized Shared Variable Mutation Inside Goroutine (Data Race)
why_it_matters: WaitGroup only coordinates goroutine completion and does not synchronize memory writes; concurrent unsynchronized mutations cause data races.

description: Detected db.Query / db.QueryContext without a corresponding defer rows.Close() cleanup call.
suggested_fix: Add defer rows.Close() immediately after checking if err != nil on QueryContext, and check rows.Err() after iteration.
title: sql.Rows Cursor Opened Without defer rows.Close()
why_it_matters: If the loop exits early due to an error or return, the underlying database connection remains checked out forever, exhausting MaxOpenConns.

description: Detected sql.Open() without SetMaxOpenConns, SetMaxIdleConns, and SetConnMaxLifetime.
title: sql.Open Initialized Without Connection Pool Bounds
why_it_matters: Default MaxOpenConns is unlimited (0), allowing traffic spikes to overwhelm PostgreSQL max_connections.

description: Detected Query, QueryRow, or Exec called without a context.Context parameter.
suggested_fix: Use the *Context variant (db.QueryContext, db.QueryRowContext, db.ExecContext) with r.Context().
title: Database Query Executed Without Context Cancellation
why_it_matters: Queries without context cannot be cancelled when an HTTP client disconnects or request times out, leading to query exhaustion.

description: Detected panic(...) call in application code.
suggested_fix: Return wrapped errors using fmt.Errorf("operation failed: %w", err) and inspect with errors.Is / errors.As.
title: Explicit panic() Used for Normal Error Handling
why_it_matters: In Go, panic unwinds the goroutine stack and terminates the process unless recovered. Errors are values and should be returned explicitly.

description: Detected fallible I/O, OS, SQL, or parsing call assigning its error return value to _.
suggested_fix: Capture and check if err != nil before using the returned value.
title: Error Return Value Explicitly Discarded With Blank Identifier (_)
why_it_matters: Proceeding after a failed os.Open, db.Exec, or json.Unmarshal causes nil-pointer dereferences or silent data corruption.

description: Network port or address defined as a fixed constant without environment variable fallback.
suggested_fix: Use an environment variable helper like envOr("PORT", "8080").
title: Hardcoded Network Port or Address Constant
why_it_matters: Prevents dynamic port binding in container and PaaS environments like Cloud Run and Kubernetes.

description: None of the configured offline static rules or AST checks matched this snippet.
suggested_fix: Run go test -race and database EXPLAIN ANALYZE for runtime verification.
title: No Static Rule Triggered in This Snippet
why_it_matters: Absence of static findings does NOT guarantee code is bug-free or secure. Concurrency races and runtime query plan bottlenecks require testing and benchmarking.

description: Detected regular expression compilation inside a function rather than at package initialization.
suggested_fix: Hoist var pattern = regexp.MustCompile(...) to package scope so it compiles once at startup.
title: regexp.MustCompile / Compile Inside Function Body
why_it_matters: Compiling a finite automaton on every request allocates dozens of heap objects and increases CPU latency by >100x.

description: Detected fmt.Sprintf or string concatenation constructing a SQL SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statement.
suggested_fix: Pass SQL parameters strictly via driver placeholders: db.QueryContext(ctx, "SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = $1", email).
title: Dynamic SQL String Concatenation / Interpolation
why_it_matters: Interpolating untrusted input directly into SQL text allows attackers to alter the SQL AST and exfiltrate or destroy database records (SQL Injection / OWASP A03 / API10).

description: Detected io.ReadAll(r.Body) or json.NewDecoder(r.Body) without prior http.MaxBytesReader limit.
suggested_fix: Wrap r.Body before reading: r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20) // 1 MiB limit.
title: Unbounded HTTP Request Body Read (Missing http.MaxBytesReader)
why_it_matters: A malicious client can stream a multi-gigabyte request body to trigger Out-Of-Memory (OOM) termination (OWASP API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption).

description: Detected http.ListenAndServe or http.Get / &http.Client{} without ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout, or Timeout.
title: Default HTTP Server / Client Without Explicit Timeouts
why_it_matters: Zero timeouts allow Slowloris clients or stalled upstream servers to hang sockets and leak goroutines indefinitely.

description: Detected blank import _ "net/http/pprof", which registers diagnostic heap/CPU profiles on http.DefaultServeMux.
suggested_fix: Bind pprof handlers explicitly to an internal loopback ServeMux on 127.0.0.1:6060.
title: Public Exposure of net/http/pprof on DefaultServeMux
why_it_matters: If DefaultServeMux is exposed publicly, attackers can download heap dumps and sensitive memory arguments (OWASP API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration).

description: Detected hardcoded secret, token, private key or password in source code.
suggested_fix: Read credentials dynamically from environment variables or secrets manager.
title: Hardcoded Secret / Credential Literal
why_it_matters: Hardcoded credentials in source control can be leaked and cannot be rotated without recompilation.

description: Confirmed syntax, type-checking, or go vet analyzer diagnostic reported directly by the Go toolchain.
suggested_fix: Fix the compilation or vet diagnostic reported at the line indicated.
title: Go Compiler / go vet Diagnostic Output
why_it_matters: Code that fails compiler or vet inspection cannot run reliably in production.
